title: Composite Scaffolds of Interfacial Polyelectrolyte Fibers for Temporally Controlled Release of Biomolecules
protocol: Purify chitosan as detailed in Liao et al.
Create a 1% (w/v) solution of chitosan in 2% (v/v) acetic acid.
Vacuum filter the solution using grade 93 filter paper.
Neutralize the filtrate with 5M NaOH until pH stabilizes to 7.
Centrifuge the precipitated chitosan at 1,200 x g for 10 min.
Decant the supernatant and add deionized water to wash the chitosan.
Repeat centrifugation and washing step two more times.
Freeze the precipitated chitosan at -80 °C and lyophilize O/N.
Store purified chitosan in a dehumidified cabinet.
Weigh out 1 g of purified chitosan into a sterile tissue culture dish.
Expose chitosan to UV light for 15 min using sterile forceps.
Place sterilized chitosan into a glass container.
Dissolve chitosan using filtered 0.15M acetic acid to a final concentration between 0.5% and 1% (w/v).
Weigh out 0.1 g of alginic acid sodium salt.
Dissolve the alginic acid sodium salt in 10 ml distilled deionized water to obtain a 1% (w/v) solution.
Mix the alginate solution for at least 2 hr on the vortex mixer to ensure complete dissolution.
Filter the alginate solution through 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Store the alginate solution at 4 °C.
Reconstitute human recombinant growth factors such as VEGF or NGF according to manufacturer recommendations.
Mix proteins, growth factors, or other biomolecules into a 10-20 µl aliquot of polyelectrolyte solution with similar net charge.
For biological molecules with net negative charge (e.g., BSA), mix them with alginate solution.
For biological molecules with net positive charge (e.g., VEGF), mix them with chitosan solution.
Place small 10-20 µl aliquots of chitosan and alginate on a stable flat surface covered with parafilm.
Lightly dip each tip on a pair of forceps into the chitosan and alginate droplets.
Bring the droplets of polyelectrolytes together by pinching the forceps.
Slowly pull the forceps vertically upward to draw IPC fiber from the interface of the two droplets.
Weigh out pullulan polysaccharide and mix with distilled deionized (DDI) water to create a 20% (w/v) aqueous solution.
Mix the pullulan solution overnight to ensure homogeneity.
Cast 15 g of pullulan solution into a 10 cm diameter tissue culture polystyrene dish.
Dry the pullulan solution overnight at 37°C.
Cut the pullulan films into 7 mm x 7 mm square frames.
Create a 30% (w/v) solution of pullulan and dextran in DDI water using a 3:1 ratio.
Mix overnight to ensure homogeneity of the polysaccharide solution.
Slowly add sodium bicarbonate to achieve a final concentration of 20% (w/v).
Mix overnight again to ensure complete mixing.
Store the polysaccharide solution at 4 °C.
Affix the sacrificial pullulan frame using an alligator clip.
Stick the alligator clip and pullulan frame on the end of the rotating mandrel with plastic-coated adhesive tape.
Rotate the mandrel with the affixed frame at a constant speed of 10 mm/sec.
Draw IPC fibers using forceps and attach one end to the rotating pullulan frame.
Draw the IPC fibers at a constant speed until reaching the terminal end of the fiber.
Dry the fibers-on-frame construct overnight at room temperature.
Mix 100 µl of 11% (w/v) sodium trimetaphosphate aqueous solution with every gram of pullulan-dextran solution.
Add 100 µl of 10M sodium hydroxide to the mixture.
Stir the solution at 60 rpm using a stirplate for 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour the viscous polysaccharide solution onto the fibers-on-frame construct to embed the IPC fibers.
Incubate the combined pullulan-dextran-IPC fibers (PD-IPC) at 60 °C for 30 min to form a chemically crosslinked composite scaffold.
Submerge the PD-IPC scaffold in 20% (w/v) acetic acid for 20 minutes to induce pore formation.
Wash PD-IPC scaffolds in 1X PBS for 5 minutes while shaking at 100 rpm.
Repeat washing step 2 times.
Freeze the PD-IPC scaffolds at -80 °C overnight.
Lyophilize the scaffolds for at least 24 hours before use.
Create a pristine polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomeric substrate using soft lithography process.
Use standard soft lithographic methods to create patterned PDMS substrates on poly(methyl methacrylate) templates with the desired topography.
Weigh out PCL and dissolve in dichloromethane to create a 0.9% (w/v) solution.
Drop 500 µl of 0.9% PCL solution for every 1 cm² area of PDMS substrate.
Allow all dichloromethane solvent to fully evaporate in the fume hood.
Repeat casting of 0.9% PCL to thicken the film to the desired thickness.
Remove the dried PCL film from the PDMS substrate.
Create a hole in the PCL frame using a suitably-sized puncher.
Affix the sacrificial PCL frame with hole on an alligator clip.
Stick the alligator clip onto the rotating mandrel using plastic-coated adhesive tape.
Attach the drawn end of the IPC fiber onto the PCL frame before starting rotation at 10 mm/sec.
After drawing, dry the fiber-on-frame construct overnight at 4 °C.
Drop 500 µl of 0.9% PCL solution onto the PDMS substrate to create a pristine or patterned PCL base, as required.
Cast multiple layers of 0.9% PCL solution to obtain a scaffold with the desired thickness.
Allow all dichloromethane solvent to fully evaporate in the fume hood.
Place the fiber-on-frame construct on top of the PCL base.
Add 0.9% PCL solution on the fiber-on-frame construct multiple times to get the desired thickness and fully embed the IPC fibers, fabricating a PCL-IPC composite scaffold.
Place composite PD-IPC or PCL-IPC scaffolds and stand-alone IPC fibers separately in a 24-well plate.
Immerse the scaffold and stand-alone IPC fibers with 500 µl of 1X PBS.
Incubate the samples at 37 °C.
Collect PBS at various time points (release media) and replace with 500 µl of 1X PBS.
Measure the amount of protein or growth factor in the release media using a BCA assay, ELISA, or other appropriate assay to calculate the cumulative release profile for the incorporated biomolecule.
Sterilize the lyophilized PD-IPC or PCL-IPC composite scaffolds using UV light in the biological safety cabinet for at least 20 min.
Use standard cell culture techniques to obtain a cell suspension of 2 x 105 cells in 200 µl growth media.
Seed the concentrated cell suspension onto the composite scaffolds.
Top-up the volume of growth media with additional growth media after 20 min to fully submerge the scaffolds.
Measure cell activity through standard techniques such as Alamar blue metabolic activity assay, PC12 neurite outgrowth assay or immunofluorescence.
